title: unified-promoter-with-adaptive-ab-lanes-and-shadow-absorption
author: Maya Thompson
description:
Motivation and summary: Add a unified promoter component that consolidates canary/A-B/shadow lane orchestration and automated rollback sequencing into a single runtime-aware controller. This PR addresses three operational gaps we saw during the SLO incident on 2026-01-29: lack of lane-level absorption for sudden shadow burst traffic, brittle A/B lanes when autoscale events shift capacity, and fragmented rollback playbooks spread across operator and control-plane code.

What this PR does: Implements a Promoter service (`promoter/controller.go`) that maintains per-lane state, calculates adaptive traffic fractions based on live capacity and recent SLO deltas, and provides a concise policy DSL for safety gates. Shadow absorption: the promoter can temporarily route a proportion of shadow traffic to a degraded-path buffer to avoid overloading primary canaries. Adaptive A/B lanes: lanes can declare a volatility score and capacity footprint; promoter adjusts weight decay and warmup windows dynamically. Rollback sequencing: integrates with the existing `rollback-oracle` to issue ordered rollback actions and emit an audit-ready decision trace.

Compatibility: Backwards compatible with existing rollout specs (legacy `canary` and `ab_test` CRs). Customers using custom orchestration plug-ins must add a thin shim (two-line adapter shown in `examples/adapter/README.md`).

Testing and validation: Unit tests added for lane weight computation, volatility scoring, and rollback sequencing. Integration harness updates in `perf/canary-harness` simulate bursty shadow traffic and capacity flaps. Manual dry-run performed in staging with internal canaries for two hours (see telemetry snapshots).

Rollout plan: 1) Merge to main gated by CI and two approvals. 2) Deploy promoter in staging with shadow-only mode for 24h. 3) Enable adaptive lane weighting for non-critical canaries (+1 percentage point per 15m). 4) Sweep to production with 3-hour observation window and human latch required for Tier-0 services.

Operational notes: Telemetry added: `promoter.lane.weight`, `promoter.lane.volatility`, `promoter.rollback.decision`, and `promoter.shadow.absorb_rate`. Alerts: new alert `PromoterHighAbsorbRate` triggers if absorb_rate > 30% for 10m and SLO error budget consumption > 2%.

Docs and follow-ups: Console UI needs a small UX to surface lane volatility (follow-up ticket ENG-3180). Also add a migration note to `docs/rollouts/migration.md`.

Checklist: - [x] Design doc (ENG-2145) referenced and linked - [x] Unit + integration tests - [x] Staging dry-run completed - [x] Telemetry and alerts wired - [x] Reviewer approvals

Related: builds on earlier work around session-affine handoffs; complements `session-anchored-shadow-pipeline` (see ENG-1981).

review_comments: Carlos Mendes: Overall looks great — two concerns: thread-safety in lane cache and the absorb buffer memory bounds. Can you add a bounded queue to shadow buffer?
Maya Thompson: Addressed both — added ring buffer with backpressure and unit test (`promoter/shadow_buffer_test.go`). Also added a comment explaining lock ordering.
Li Wei: CI flaked on the integration harness (timeout on canary_scenario). Reran tests and they passed. Recommend squash on merge.
Jordan Patel: Please add a brief note to runbook about human latch for Tier-0 services. I opened ENG-3180 to track console work.
